messages:
janet: Heads-up — hit a bad spot-wave in us-west2 last night. ~30% of rerank pods went Pending, CA spun up two gpu nodes that got preempted immediately, left us with a pile of CrashLoopBackOffs. Opening thread to track mitigation.

matt: Confirmed. GCE preemption events show both nodes reclaimed within ~90s of creation. CA then triggered another scale-up because pods had required nodeSelector gpu=true. End result: oscillation.

sarah: From pod events it looks like kubelet started eviction/cordon while CA was still deciding. PDBs blocked graceful eviction, so pods flapped. We should avoid full eviction/replace on every preempt signal.

kevin: Quick idea: prefer preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity for non-critical replica sets so CA can place on on-demand fallback instead of insisting on spot. That buys time without changing app code.

elaine: Cost note: when fallback to on-demand happened for ~4h we estimate an extra ~$2.2k. For customer-facing low-latency pipelines that might be acceptable, but for background batch jobs it's not. Need a policy per workload class.

matt: Operational mitigation proposal: 1) add a small cross-zone warm pool of on-demand GPUs with soft-affinity to rerank, 2) change CA expander to least-waste to reduce oscillation, 3) implement "staged cordon" on preempt: mark unschedulable but delay eviction 30-60s to allow warm pool placement.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-4528 — /incidents/INC-4528 (investigating spot preempt wave in us-west2).

janet: Draft of the staged cordon hook (pseudo-yaml):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: preempt-hook-example
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/on-demand
            operator: In
            values: ["true"]
```
And CA flags we should test: `--scale-down-delay=15m` -> `--scale-down-delay=5m` in staging, and expander=least-waste.

kevin: Also recommend adding a simple admission webhook that rewrites strict nodeSelector to preferredAffinity for job types that are non-blocking. Low-effort and avoids repo-wide changes.

sarah: I'll run a canary in us-west2-staging tomorrow 03:00-05:00 with the expander + staged cordon hook + a warm pool (2 nodes). Will monitor pod Pending %, schedule latency, and cost. If schedule failures >5% or CPU throttling >20% we rollback.

matt: I'll put together a short script to listen for GCE preemption notices and trigger the staged cordon + move annotation to allow immediate fallback. Will also add metrics for "preempt-handled" vs "preempt-failed".

elaine: I'll do a quick cost delta and customer-impact runbook. If warm pool costs >$600/day we need to consider autosize thresholds.

janet: OK owners set: sarah (canary + metrics), matt (preempt hook + automation), kevin (affinity admission webhook), elaine (cost + runbook). Reconvene after canary (add notes to INC-4528). :thumbsup:

ops-deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deployment: us-west2-staging 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z -> 2026-03-19T05:00:00Z. Config refs: gitRedwood/infra#pr-768.

matt: one more ask — let's prioritize patching the CA image (we're on 1.26.0; upstream has a 1.26.3 fix for eviction loop). Canary will include upgraded CA.

janet: Good catch. Include CA upgrade in the canary plan. We'll validate and close INC-4528 if canary stabilizes.
